amendments.why: Rule 102's own text scopes its substantival branch to a **substantival adjective**, and this chapter met the identity pronoun αὐτός twice (τὰ αὐτά at 3:1, τῷ αὐτῷ at 3:16) with nowhere in the rule to go. Both verses went wrong, and in two different directions: 3:1 handed the supplied *things* to the pronoun under rule 17's generic-noun clause, and 3:16 marked the supplied *rule* `added` under rule 5 — while 3:19 and 3:21 read the identical shape the article's way. A cross-reference would have left the over-narrow sentence in place, so the scope is widened where it stands. The widening is what rule 17 already states for the quantifier (τὰ πάντα → *all things* is the article's *things* and the quantifier's *all*) and what rule 60 already implies for αὐτός (it refuses to read the identity pronoun as a demonstrative, giving αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ → *that very hour* the article's own *that*), so no rule 49 emptying is in question; rule 103's article arm supplies the rest. Nothing else in the rule is altered, including its unanimity counts and the JAS.1.11 head correction.
amendments.rule: An article that governs an **expressed** noun is not thereby barred from taking a nominal the ASV supplies inside its own phrase, and rule 22's *never the determiner* is not scoped to a substantival article. Where the ASV writes a determiner plus a supplied noun in front of the article's own noun, both words are the article's and the unit heads on the **supplied noun**: `τοῦ κυρίου` → *the kingdom* of gives the anaphoric nominal and the case preposition to the article and leaves `κυρίου` a bare *Lord* at REV.11.15, as `τῆς δόξης` → *the Lord* does, and as `τὴν … αἰώνιον` → *the life* does at 1JN.1.2, whose note records in terms that rule 49 does not reach an article governing an expressed head noun. Rule 60's closing clause already says the head follows the nominal wherever the article supplies one, `τῆς μελλούσης` → *that hour which* heading on *hour*; this rule is that clause holding for a supplied noun as well as a supplied determiner. The same holds where the article's complement is a **substantival adjective** and no noun is expressed at all: rule 49 gives the article both the determiner and the supplied noun, so `τὸν πτωχόν` → *the … man* and `τὰ ἐπιτήδεια` → *the things* and *needful* leave the adjective bare, headed on *man* and *things*. **Adjective** there names the ordinary case and is not a scope. The complement may equally be a substantival **quantifier** or the identity pronoun **`αὐτός`**, and the supplied nominal is the article's in either: `τὰ πάντα` → *all things* gives *things* to the article and a bare *all* to the quantifier, which is what rule 17 already says of that phrase in terms, and `τὰ αὐτά` → *the same things* gives the discontinuous *the … things* to the article under rule 15 and a bare *same* to the pronoun, as `τῷ αὐτῷ` → *by that same rule* gives *by that … rule* to the article, headed on *rule*, and a bare *same* to the pronoun. Rule 49 does not empty an article before `αὐτός`: what rule 49 empties an article for is a **demonstrative** that has taken its determiner, and rule 60 has already refused to read the identity pronoun as one, giving `αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ` → *that very hour* the article's own *that* and the intensive pronoun only *very*. Rule 103's article arm is what keeps such a supplied nominal from being `added`, however plainly the phrase is elliptical and whether or not the ASV italicizes the word. Rule 17's generic-noun clause is the contrast and is scoped to **anarthrous** Greek, where no article competes and the supplied noun is a rule 7 helper on the adjective — `πτωχός` → *a poor man* heads on *poor*, as rule 58's `νεκρῶν` → *the dead* and rule 51's anarthrous clause have it, and as an anarthrous `πάντα` → *all things* heads on *all*. So the test is whether a Greek article stands to take the determiner, exactly the test rules 51 and 58 already use, and a verse writing both shapes decides each on its own article. The corpus is unanimous: all fifty-three units of an article taking a determiner plus a nominal head on the nominal and none on *the*, and every unit finalized since rule 49 entered the contract reads the substantival-adjective shape the article's way, twelve to none. JAS.1.11 corrected this very head from *the* to *man* and JAS.1.25 repeats it, so do not read rule 17's unqualified wording as reaching a phrase an article governs. What the article takes is a **supplied** nominal, and rule 66's test is what identifies one: a word that completes the phrase and glosses no element of the adjective's own lexeme, as *man*, *part* and *things* do. Where the ASV instead renders the substantival adjective by a **multiword expression of its own**, every content word of which answers to that lexeme, no word of it is supplied and this rule has nothing to hand over: the article takes only the determiner, with any case preposition riding along under rule 21, and the whole expression stays with the adjective, headed under rule 66 on the word that glosses the lexeme rather than on the phrase's formal English head. `τῷ παραλυτικῷ` → *to the sick of the palsy* gives *to the* to the article and *sick of the palsy* to the adjective headed on *palsy*, as the same phrase does where the ASV writes *unto the sick of the palsy*. `ὁ κωφός` → *the … man* with a bare *dumb* is the contrast, *man* glossing no element of `κωφός`; and the anarthrous `παραλυτικόν` → *a man sick of the palsy* is rule 17's case, where no article competes and the completion stays with the adjective too. So ask of each English word whether it completes the phrase or renders the lexeme before handing any of it to the article, and never split one lexeme's own English between the article and the adjective in order to give the article a noun.

conventions: A supplied English nominal completing a phrase a Greek article governs belongs to the article, headed on the nominal, whatever the complement's class, and is neither the complement's nor `added`: τὰ ἐπίγεια → *earthly things* (3:19) and τὰ πάντα → *all things* (3:8, 3:21) give *things* to the article and a bare *earthly* or *all* to the complement, and the identity pronoun αὐτός is no different — τὰ αὐτά → *the … things* / *same* (3:1) and τῷ αὐτῷ → *by that … rule* / *same* (3:16), the italics on *rule* being evidence only, since the ASV's own text lacked κανόνι and the selected reading agrees with it. The contrast is anarthrous Greek, where no article competes and the completion stays with the complement: ἄλλος → *other man* heads on *other* (3:4), and the anarthrous πάντα → *all things* heads on *all* in the same verse as the articular τὰ πάντα (3:8). Where the ASV supplies no nominal the article keeps only what was written, so Τὸ λοιπόν → *Finally* leaves it `unrepresented` (3:1).

A supplied English predicate frame — complementizer, subject pronoun and copula together — rides with the standing token it is predicated of and is not `added`: *that they are* goes to the predicate noun ἐχθρούς (3:18) and *that it may be* to the predicate adjective σύμμορφον (3:21), the article keeping only its own determiner. It is `added` only where no token stands to be predicated of, as at 3:13, where the ASV supplies both subject and lexical verb over an accusative object — *one thing I do* — and ἕν is that verb's object rather than its predicate. The test is what the supplied verb predicates of, not whether its English subject is supplied: at 3:18 the subject is supplied too.

report: Checked all 36 candidate lemma groups, and read the dump end to end for the split the lemma table cannot see (the kind with an `added` side). Two real splits; four verses patched (3:1, 3:8, 3:16, 3:18).

Split 1 — a supplied English nominal completing a phrase a Greek article governs was analysed four ways: given to the article at 3:19 (τὰ ἐπίγεια → *things* / *earthly*) and 3:21 (τὰ πάντα → *things* / *all*); given to the complement at 3:1 (τὰ αὐτά → *the* / *same things*); left with the article `unrepresented` at 3:8 (τὰ πάντα); and marked `added` at 3:16 (τῷ αὐτῷ → *rule*). Rules 17, 102 and 103 settle it for the article — rule 17 names τὰ πάντα → *all things* in terms as the article's *things* and the quantifier's *all*. Patched 3:1, 3:8 and 3:16 to the 3:19/3:21 reading, each headed on the supplied nominal.

3:16's *rule* is not a rule 97 case and the note now says so: the ASV italicizes it because the ASV's own text lacked κανόνι, and SBLGNT.PHP.3.16.v010 selected r00-base agrees with it, so no reading the ASV translated has been excluded. Rule 11 makes the italics evidence, and rule 103's article arm folds the word.

Split 2, invisible to the lemma table because one side is `added` — a supplied predicate frame (complementizer, subject pronoun, copula) rides with the predicate at 3:21 (σύμμορφον → *that it may be conformed*) but was `added` at 3:18 (*that they are* over the predicate noun ἐχθρούς). Rules 63, 68, 85, 92 and 96 fold it, and rule 62 says in terms that it leaves 68 and 96 untouched wherever a standing token is what the supplied verb predicates of. Patched 3:18; the article keeps its own *the* between, discontinuously under rule 15.

The `added` frame at 3:13 (*one thing I do*) stands and is not the same case: ἕν is that supplied verb's object rather than its predicate, and the subject is supplied too, which is rule 62's own test for `added`.

Checked and found licensed, not split: the T→PREP articles reproduce rule 31's own examples — 3:6 κατὰ δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐν νόμῳ (article follows its noun, takes only the relativizer) and 3:9 τὴν ἐκ θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην (article precedes, takes the discontinuous *the … which*) — with 3:11 `unrepresented` because the ASV writes no relative clause there. 3:19's three parallel ὧν clauses differ because only two express the pronoun, so rules 20 and 76 give the third's supplied *whose* to the article. 3:3 and 3:19 write one English word for a substantival article before a participle (rule 90) while 3:17 writes two and splits (rule 32). μέν and καί differ by what the ASV wrote (rules 65, 70). 3:4's anarthrous ἄλλος → *other man* headed on *other* is the correct contrast to the articular cases, not a third treatment.

BSB: none of the three disagreements is an error. 3:10 τῆς and τῷ are articles whose determiner αὐτοῦ displaced (rule 20's own example shape, *of his resurrection*, *unto his death*), and 3:21 τοῦ is the nominalizing article of an articular infinitive (rule 61). All three are the documented convention difference; nothing was changed for them.
After the patches: 338 units (was 340), aligned 315, unrepresented 20, added 3. Every source and target id in each patched verse is partitioned exactly once.
